book.title: The New Penguin Book of The Guardian Crosswords, volume 11

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it, so the road goes within the mess

parts.note: to make a hash of something is to make a mess of it
the M1 motorway, written MI in crosswords, is Britain's best-known road

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's road is in a terrible state.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'. Hamish is the Scottish form of James, so it serves as a typical Scot's name, like Jock.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamish is a stereotypically Scottish first name, used in crosswords to stand for any Scotsman.

clue.text: Puts about paper nearer the source

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are moved around into a different order

parts.note: taken as written
a ream is a quantity of paper, 500 sheets

explanation.surface: Someone moves a newspaper closer to where a story came from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puts about' reads like a phrasal verb, as in spreading a rumour, but 'about' works on the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling up a river takes you towards where it rises, so going upstream brings you closer to its spring.

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
deal is pine or fir timber
surface padding: the two pieces run together as one made-up name

explanation.surface: It reads like the headline name of a famous court case, the Goldwood Trial.
explanation.walkthrough: Goldwood looks like a surname in a case title, but it splits into two words for the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a painful experience that tests someone, and historically trial by ordeal was a judicial test.

clue.text: Cover for Tom in book this taxi controller should do

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the hut where Uncle Tom lives in Harriet Beecher Stowe's novel Uncle Tom's Cabin
second meaning, read as a phrase: a taxi dispatcher should record each car arriving back

explanation.surface: An odd instruction mixing a book character's shelter with a cab firm's duties.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as three words, LOG CAB IN, and it is what a dispatcher does when a taxi returns.
explanation.definitionFit: A log cabin is a rough hut built from tree trunks, the shelter of the slave Tom in Stowe's novel.

parts.note: the clue is the result; the answer describes how to get it from onus, a word for duty or burden, with its end trimmed

explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the clue word is what the answer's instruction produces. Onus means responsibility, and cutting its last letter diminishes it to ONU.
explanation.definitionFit: Diminished responsibility is a legal plea that a defendant's mental state lessened their culpability for a crime.

clue.text: Five years taken over plain star

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: taken over suggests turning something over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: an age is a long span of years

explanation.surface: An unremarkable star takes five years to be noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: Plain looks like an adjective describing the star, but it is a second definition: vega is a Spanish word for a fertile plain.
explanation.definitionFit: Vega is the brightest star in the constellation Lyra, and in Spanish-speaking regions a vega is a fertile lowland.

parts.note: surface reading: a stubborn farm animal is not kept somewhere heated
setter's reading: a mule is also a backless slipper, so this is a warmer for the hands, not the feet

explanation.surface: A farmer explains that the donkey-horse cross isn't kept somewhere heated.
explanation.walkthrough: Mule suggests the animal, but it is the slipper. A slipper keeps feet warm; the answer is a warmer that hands go into instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A muff is a tube of fur or fabric into which both hands are pushed to keep them cosy.

parts.note: an arrow on a sign indicates the way; to arrow is to point out
to sing and to grass both mean to inform to the police

explanation.surface: A songbook direction: perform 'Sing in the Marsh'.
explanation.walkthrough: Sing and grass are both underworld slang for informing on someone. The definition is loose: something found growing in the marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrowgrass is a rush-like plant of wet ground and salt marshes, so it is a thing growing there.

parts.note: surface reading: the French word for seasoning on food
setter's reading: the English salad term put into French clothes, which is what this word is

explanation.walkthrough: The clue is written in French, so it is both the condiment and an English word dressed up in French.
explanation.definitionFit: French dressing is a vinaigrette of oil and vinegar for salads, a kind of seasoning poured over food.

clue.text: Caesar's murder wasn't made out with turn

definitions.note: the answer completes the sentence: Caesar's murder wasn't undreamt

indicators.note: out suggests letters thrown out of their usual order and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A historical note that Caesar's assassination was not carried out with a twist.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare, Caesar's wife Calpurnia dreamt of his murder the night before, so it was not something nobody had dreamt of.
explanation.definitionFit: Undreamt means never imagined; Calpurnia's dream of the killing means it was foreseen, completing the sentence.

definitions.note: read as two words, the answer split LESS ON
definitions.meaning: first meaning, split in two: someone barer is wearing fewer clothes
second meaning: a single period of teaching

explanation.surface: Asking which bit of schooling is the most basic.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as LESS ON: someone barer has less on, and the whole word is a unit of teaching.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesson is one period of teaching, a single unit in a course of schooling.

clue.text: One of the hellish Women's Lib's partners holding the aces

indicators.note: something holding another has it within its grasp, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the Liberals' partners were the Social Democrats, together the Lib Dems
an ace counts as one

explanation.surface: Women's Lib campaigners clinging on to their best cards.
explanation.walkthrough: Women's Lib looks like one phrase, but the break comes after Women. The Liberal Democrats are a UK party formed from the Liberals and Social Democrats.
explanation.definitionFit: A demoness is a female demon, so she is one of the women of hell.

clue.text: Sportsman or railwayman not getting in late

indicators.note: not getting in means being left out, so that word is dropped from the longer one

parts.note: a platelayer lays and maintains railway track
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sportsman or a railway worker who never manages to clock in late.
explanation.walkthrough: A platelayer is the British term for a railway track worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is anyone who takes part in a sport or game, especially as a professional.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to cover the eyes, or a covering that does so
second meaning: a gangster, short for hoodlum, or Robin of Sherwood
third meaning: a cloth head covering, and the US word for a car's bonnet

explanation.surface: A sightless bandit's hat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers a head covering, a car's engine cover, a cover over the eyes, and a slang gangster.

clue.text: Where to find Her Majesty's exam paper?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as two words: ER, the Queen, sits in the middle of the word term
second meaning: a test sat halfway through a school or college term

explanation.surface: Asking where the Queen's examination script has been put.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen; split the answer MID TERM and those letters are its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A midterm is an examination held in the middle of an academic term, chiefly in American schools.

parts.note: surface reading: an order to curtsey or nod to someone ignorant of the sea
setter's reading: what a non-sailor calls the front of a ship

explanation.walkthrough: Bow looks like a verb of greeting, but it is the front of a boat; a landlubber has no nautical words and describes it plainly.
explanation.definitionFit: The pointed front part of a vessel, named informally by someone who does not know the proper term.

indicators.note: the apostrophe shows the opening h dropped, in Cockney fashion, so the same is done to the hollow

parts.note: a profiter is one who profits or gains
a hole is a hollow

explanation.surface: A Cockney describes a cake that has a hollow inside.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, the pastry itself is hollow, a choux shell filled with cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A profiterole is a small ball of choux paste filled with cream and usually topped with chocolate.

indicators.note: heard means we go by how the word is said, not how it is spelt

parts.note: a toxin is a poisoner's stock in trade

explanation.surface: A poisoner hears the alarm being raised.
explanation.definitionFit: A tocsin is an old word for a warning bell rung to raise an alarm, or any warning signal.

parts.note: surface reading: the idiom for a tiny, insignificant amount
setter's reading: a literal fall in the level of the sea

explanation.walkthrough: The familiar idiom about something too small to matter is read literally, as the sea's level going down.
explanation.definitionFit: The outgoing tide, when sea levels fall between high water and low water twice daily.

clue.text: Dives where I, by reaching up, dip into glossies

indicators.note: to dip into is to go inside, so these pieces sit within the other

parts.note: glossies are glossy magazines, mags

indicators.note: in a down entry, reaching up means the word runs bottom to top, read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
I as a Roman numeral is one

explanation.surface: Someone dives into glossy magazines, stretching up to dip into them.
explanation.walkthrough: Dives is not the verb: it is the rich man in the Bible parable of Dives and Lazarus, the name being Latin for rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Moneybags is a slang term for a wealthy person, and Dives is the archetypal rich man.

clue.text: 12. I know what'll happen if all one runs on's up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: the sum is the whole lot
a means one
darts are quick runs
taken as written

explanation.surface: A seer boasts that he can predict what happens when everyone runs out of road.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue speaks in the voice of the answer, the famous prophet, and 12 is the entry's own number, naming him.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostradamus was the 16th-century French astrologer whose verse prophecies claim to foretell the future.

clue.text: Bewilder knight discovered embracing spy chief

indicators.note: embracing means wrapping arms around, so one piece holds another inside

parts.note: to dub is to make someone a knight with a tap of the sword
M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories
found is a synonym of discovered

explanation.surface: A knight is found out hugging the head of espionage, to everyone's confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: Knight looks like a noun, but here it is a verb, to dub. The knight piece holds the chief, and the find comes afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To dumbfound is to astonish someone so much that they are left speechless and confused.

parts.note: egging someone on is encouraging them
the Inferno is Dante's hell

explanation.surface: China that urges on a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggshell porcelain is a very thin, translucent china, so delicate it is named after the shell.

clue.text: It's Frank, a brother for nothing!

definitions.note: the answer is a noun for the quality of being frank

parts.note: anything for nothing costs nothing
Dom is the title of a Benedictine monk, a religious brother

explanation.surface: Someone introduces Frank, a brother who asks nothing in return.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank looks like a man's name; it is the adjective, and freedom of speech or manner is frankness.
explanation.definitionFit: Freedom can mean openness or outspokenness in speech or behaviour, the state of being candid.

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something in another is placed inside it

parts.note: my and heavens are both exclamations of surprise
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: A cry of delight about a house in paradise, then a puzzled 'Pardon?'.
explanation.walkthrough: Pardon? looks like a request to repeat something; it is the definition, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An amnesty is an official pardon granted to a group of offenders, often by a government.

parts.note: scree is loose broken rock on a mountain slope
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Loose stones lying against a partition on the north side.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen is a movable panel used to divide off part of a room, a kind of partition.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang for a one-pound note or coin
second meaning: something outstanding or unusually big

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at a huge price of a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Oner is British slang both for a single pound sterling and for something remarkable or exceptional of its kind.
